newsitem.title: USA: Shrine to "murdered" cat prompts U.S. court order.
newsitem.headline: Shrine to "murdered" cat prompts U.S. court order.

text.p: A six-foot (two metre) shrine to Scrappy -- "murdered for being a cat" -- has so much fur flying in South Carolina that a court had to order two warring neighbours to keep apart.

Sheryl Jones set up the white crucifix in her front yard after neighbours Becky and David Williams called in the animal squad on Oct. 11 to deal with Scrappy, who kept coming into their yard from Jones' property. Animal shelter officials, claiming the cat was wild and had tried to bite workers, euthanized it the same day.
Jones set up her monument to Scrappy with the epitaph: "In memory of Scrappy, murdered for being a cat. 1985-1996." She lights candles on top of the cross at night.
In a court hearing on Wednesday, Becky Williams alleged Jones had also attempted to run her off the road, threatened her family and dog and called her a murderer.
Richland County Magistrate Michael Davis issued a restraining order barring Jones and her daughter Rose, 16, from going on the Williams' property or harassing them.
"You're going to have to live as neighbours," he said. "Hopefully over a period of time this situation will calm down between the two of you."
